description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04, two PRINCIPAL flags in succession)

PRINCIPAL flagged twice in fast succession during the arc-21 cluster work:
1. 'Ok, get your shit together...if we are running a team in autonomous mode they all need to be autonomous.'
2. 'This is something that needs to be cooked into the stoa...to run either autonomously or human in the loop and all the agents need to understand how that works including the nested projects.'

The Stoa substrate currently has Mode 1 (formal gauntlet) and Mode 2 (prototyping pairing) as operating modes per §12. Those describe WHAT the team is doing. PRINCIPAL is asking for an orthogonal dimension: HOW PRINCIPAL participates — autonomous (PRINCIPAL is exception-handler only) or human-in-the-loop (PRINCIPAL is active participant in routine flow).

This needs to be cooked into substrate so every POLYBIUS at every tier inherits the capability AND the convention to propagate the mode declaration down to its team.

## The substrate concept (proposed)

Two operating engagements, orthogonal to Mode 1/Mode 2:

- **Human-in-the-loop (HITL) — default for new engagements.** Agents surface to PRINCIPAL for routine direction. More chat round-trips. PRINCIPAL is active participant. Lower context cost per agent. Higher PRINCIPAL attention cost.

- **Autonomous — explicitly declared.** Agents handle their own stuff via bw coordination + polling crons + radio-check protocols. PRINCIPAL is exception-handler (project-direction calls, ship/no-ship, ambiguity, peer-failure escalations). Higher per-agent context cost (cron fires, polling). Lower PRINCIPAL attention cost.

Mode transitions:
- HITL → Autonomous: PRINCIPAL declares ('go autonomous', 'step back', similar). The seat receiving the declaration runs the autonomous-mode-setup checklist (per stoa--ljf) AND propagates the mode declaration down the tier hierarchy. Their PLINY (when dispatched) inherits autonomous mode. Their CAPTAINs (when dispatched) inherit. Their sub-project POLYBIUSes (if any) inherit AND propagate further down.
- Autonomous → HITL: PRINCIPAL declares ('come back', 'I want to be in the loop', similar). All affected seats stop polling crons + radio-check, return to chat-first interaction.

## Propagation across nested tiers

If user-tier POLYBIUS goes autonomous on an engagement that involves project-tier work:
- Project-tier POLYBIUS for that engagement is also autonomous by default
- Their PLINY-when-dispatched inherits autonomous
- Their CAPTAINs-when-dispatched inherit autonomous
- Sub-project POLYBIUSes-of-that-project inherit autonomous

If a sub-project's work needs human-in-the-loop while the parent is autonomous, the sub-project POLYBIUS can declare HITL for its sub-engagement (downward override). Reverse override (sub goes autonomous when parent is HITL) is unusual and requires explicit PRINCIPAL declaration.

## Parents of this epic (sibling concerns this unifies)

The arc-21 cluster (now 10+ tickets) is the operational mechanism for autonomous mode. This META-ticket is the substrate concept they instantiate.

- stoa--vz9 (operating disciplines — provides the team-wide framing layer this can extend)
- stoa--ivc (radio-check pattern — autonomous-mode peer detection)
- stoa--ay1 (adaptive polling cadence — autonomous-mode efficiency)
- stoa--blg (cross-tier write boundaries — autonomous-mode data flow)
- stoa--xh2 (activation paste filename divergence — affects autonomous activation)
- stoa--m5m (positive-references-only directive discipline — autonomous activation)
- stoa--0mr (bw storage model — needed for any mode)
- stoa--cc0 (unified polling pattern — autonomous-mode cron architecture)
- stoa--1n5 (cross-tier coordination convention — autonomous-mode routing)
- stoa--ljf (autonomous-mode-setup checklist — autonomous-mode activation)
- THIS TICKET (the unifying meta concept)

Proposed: arc-21 design covers all 11 as one comprehensive substrate update. Single arc directive, multi-concern, requires §5.4 external review. POLYBIUS_the_stoa drives.

## Where in substrate

1. **MAJOR_POLYBIUS §12 (or new §13)** — add Operating-engagement axis (HITL vs Autonomous) alongside the Mode 1/Mode 2 framing.

2. **operating-disciplines.md** — universal team protocol; both modes apply to every seat.

3. **substrate/templates/** — paste-instruction templates parameterize HITL vs Autonomous. Default HITL.

4. **MAJOR_PLINY §x** — gauntlet dispatch in autonomous mode runs differently (less PRINCIPAL surfacing per round) than HITL. Document.

5. **Each CAPTAIN role file** — note that they receive operating-mode in their dispatch brief and act accordingly.

## Trigger words for mode transition

PRINCIPAL declares mode via natural language. Recognized triggers (substrate teaches POLYBIUS to detect):

HITL → Autonomous: 'go autonomous', 'step back', 'you can handle this', 'I'll be away', 'work autonomously until X'
Autonomous → HITL: 'come back', 'I want to be in the loop', 'pause autonomous', 'let me decide each step'

When detected, the seat receiving the declaration runs setup/teardown procedures + propagates downward.

## Reference

- 2026-05-04 ariadne--m20 + arc-21 cluster engagements
- §12 of MAJOR_POLYBIUS (Mode 1 / Mode 2 framing — orthogonal axis)
- u--7yg (chief-of-staff discipline accretion epic on user-beadwork — parallel discipline-accretion at user-tier)
title: [META] Operating modes (autonomous vs human-in-the-loop) as substrate first-class concept across all tiers including nested
